scope: Tracing out spectator coordinates produces a positive two-particle density operator of trace one from every physical N-fermion density operator.
The set of representable two-particle densities is convex, and tracing out one spectator proves the nesting of these sets with increasing particle number (note 27).
Relabeling antisymmetric particle coordinates preserves the density when applied on both indices. The last-particle partial trace preserves antisymmetry of the remaining state.
A two-body observable on any chosen ordered particle pair has expectation equal to its trace against the normalized pair density.

The attainable energies of a finite N-fermion Hamiltonian that sums two-body terms are exactly the attainable values of the linear energy functional on representable two-particle marginals. This is the variational identity used in the hardness reduction.
Gershgorin bounds the Hermitian trace norm by dimension squared times the largest entry. Explicit Hermitian two-body observables read the real or imaginary entry.

For a candidate at trace-norm distance at least β from all representable pair densities, an explicit pair observable distinguishes it from every convex mixture of physical block marginals with signal exceeding β/(4d⁴).
The expectation discrepancy of a bounded verifier statistic forces a rejection probability lower bound for arbitrary correlated finite measurement outcomes.
